analysis.one_liner: Bosch Ltd makes automotive components (fuel-injection and power-train systems, sensors, two-wheeler electronics) in India and is majority owned by Germany's Robert Bosch group.
tags: Q1 profit had a one-off gain
analysis.whats_happening: On 6 November 2026 the board announced results for the quarter ended September 2026 together with a 1:5 stock split and a 3:1 bonus issue (together turning 1 share into 20); the record date is not yet fixed and the action needs shareholder approval via postal ballot. Consolidated PAT rose about 18-19% year-on-year to roughly Rs 840 crore, while standalone PAT was Rs 554.5 crore, up only 3.3% YoY, on revenue of Rs 4,795 crore (+9.1% YoY). The stock has fallen about 5.6% from its 5 November peak, with several reports describing the reaction as a 'sell the news' move on the split/bonus plus a weaker-than-expected quarter-on-quarter profit comparison.
analysis.plain_terms: A stock split and bonus issue just multiply the number of shares you hold by 20 - they do not add any value, and the share price will fall proportionately once the record date passes. Separately, don't be fooled by the headline profit numbers this year: the previous quarter's profit was inflated by a one-time gain from selling a business unit, so comparing this quarter to that one makes normal operations look weak when they are not. The real tension is that Bosch trades at a rich valuation (P/E near 56x) that assumes steady, high-quality growth, but the underlying operating margin has been flat to slightly down.
analysis.quarters: The quarter ended June 2026 reported standalone/consolidated PAT of about Rs 1,115 crore, up ~140% YoY - but Rs 556 crore of that was an exceptional gain from selling Bosch's video-surveillance and access-control business to Keenfinity India; profit before tax excluding that item was up a more modest 37% YoY. The quarter ended September 2026 normalised: standalone PAT was Rs 554.5 crore (+3.3% YoY, down ~50% QoQ purely because the prior quarter had the one-off gain), on revenue up 9.1% YoY. Management's call cited two-wheeler revenue up 81.8% on OBD2 emission-norm-driven demand for sensors, power solutions (diesel components) up 11.5%, aftermarket growth slowing to 4.5% after a GST rate cut, and consumer goods growing just 1.8% on adverse forex and input costs. These are non-comparable quarter-to-quarter because of the exceptional item - treat the June 2026 quarter's reported PAT growth figure as not representative of underlying trends.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year the stock is up 33.8% versus Nifty's -2.1%, but it lagged its peer Motherson's 58.7%. Over 3 years it is up 161% versus Nifty's 29% but again behind the peer's 179%. Over 5 years it is up 183%, ahead of both Nifty (39%) and the peer (155%). The one historical corporate action (a 10:1 split in 2004) is already reflected in these adjusted return series, so it does not distort them. The newly announced 1:5 split plus 3:1 bonus has not yet taken effect (record date pending) - once it does, expect the quoted share price to drop sharply on a chart; that will be a mechanical adjustment, not a loss of value, and should be read alongside the new share count.
analysis.valuation_read: Bosch trades at roughly 56x earnings and about 19.5x book value, well above the auto components sector median P/E of around 31x. Why it looks expensive: a 19.3% ROE and 25.6% ROCE, both comfortably above sector medians, plus scarcity value as one of the few listed, nearly pure MNC-parented auto component franchises with strong brand and engineering pedigree. Whether it is actually cheap is a separate question - at this multiple there is little room for disappointment, and part of recent profit growth has come from an exceptional one-off gain rather than core operations, which investors should strip out before judging the multiple.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue grew about 9% YoY in the latest quarter, driven by volumes (particularly two-wheeler sensor demand tied to OBD2 norms and power-solutions/diesel component demand) rather than margin expansion - core operating margin excluding other income was roughly flat to slightly down quarter-on-quarter at 12.87%. This is volume-led growth, and the consumer goods segment (just 1.8% growth) is a drag, so the overall growth picture is mixed rather than broad-based.
analysis.health_read: Reported ROCE (25.6%) and ROE (19.3%) both point to profits that are being generated efficiently on capital employed; Bosch is typically run as a low-leverage MNC subsidiary in India. Not verified - check Screener for the exact current net debt/cash position and operating cash flow conversion. The more relevant risk here looks like business risk (demand mix across auto segments, forex exposure in consumer goods) rather than financial/leverage risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters - led by Robert Bosch Internationale Beteiligungen AG, part of the German Bosch Group - hold about 70.54% of the company, with zero shares pledged as of the most recent disclosure. The remaining float is split among mutual funds (6.67%), insurance companies (7.65%), FIIs (7.10%), DIIs (0.84%) and retail investors (7.19%). There is no well-known individual or marquee domestic investor on the shareholder register - this is a promoter-and-institution-held stock, not one with a retail-star following.
strengths: ROCE of 25.6% and ROE of 19.3%, both above the sector median (14.96% and 12.55% respectively)
Promoter holding of 70.54% with zero pledging, signalling no financial stress at the parent level
Two-wheeler segment revenue up 81.8% YoY on OBD2 emission-norm-driven sensor demand
5-year return of 183%, ahead of both Nifty (39%) and peer Motherson (155%) over that horizon
watchpoints: P/E of ~56x versus a sector median of ~31x leaves little margin for error if growth disappoints
The quarter ended June 2026's Rs 1,115 crore profit included a Rs 556 crore one-off gain from selling the video-surveillance/access-control business to Keenfinity - don't extrapolate that growth rate
Consumer goods segment grew just 1.8% YoY, hurt by adverse forex and input costs

A 1:5 stock split plus 3:1 bonus issue is pending (record date not yet fixed) - once effective, the per-share price will drop mechanically to about 1/20th; this is a share-count change, not a value change
analysis.one_thing: Whether standalone operating margin (excluding other income and exceptional items) holds above the ~13% seen pre-this-quarter or stabilises nearer the 11.5% reported this quarter will show if the latest dip is a one-off or the new normal; the bonus/split record date announcement is the other near-term event to watch.
analysis.data_notes: PAT and revenue figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, MarketsMojo, Deccan Herald and Sahi.com; standalone and consolidated figures diverge by a wide margin and could not be fully reconciled from available sources - check Screener for a clean standalone-vs-consolidated and segment-level breakdown. Different outlets use inconsistent fiscal-year labels (some call the September 2026 quarter 'Q2 FY26', others 'Q2 FY27') - quarters above are described by calendar month to avoid ambiguity.
